evidence.quote: List all organization members. Response includes pending invites that are approved by organization owners or managers but waiting to be accepted by the invitee.
Returns a paginated list of members bound to a organization with a SCIM Users GET Request.

assumptions: The source did not describe how pagination works for the members list. I assumed Sentry's standard Link-header cursor paging, which is not confirmed here.

The organization is taken as the first one returned by the 'List Your Organizations' call (path 0.slug, since the response is a top-level list). If the token can see several organizations, the wrong one may be picked.
The region (us or de) must be supplied by the customer as a connection setting.
The source did not say how to read suspended or deactivated members. Status is only derived from the pending-invite flag (pending or active), so suspended users are not distinguished.
Last activity comes from the user's lastActive field, falling back to lastLogin. Pending invites have no linked user, so they will have no activity date.
I assumed the response is a top-level array and used '$' as the records path.
No rate limit information was given in the source.

The source said little about auth. I assumed a Sentry auth token sent as a Bearer token with member:read scope. An internal integration token would survive staff leaving better than a user token, but this was not confirmed.
The organization slug from the first context step is now stored under the name 'org' and used as {{context.org}}; I could not confirm the runtime's exact naming rule for context values.
